_comment: Checked-in capability policy for the cross-SDK suite (read by orchestrator/test_runner.py).
Every capability a scenario lists under `requires` must appear in `capabilities`, and every SDK
must classify every capability as either `required` (the wrapper MUST advertise it as true; a
false/missing value fails the run and the gated scenarios still execute) or a reviewed
`unsupported` exception with a one-line reason (the gated scenarios are skipped). A capability
that is neither, or an SDK with no entry here, fails closed. Extra keys a wrapper returns from
/capabilities that are not listed in `capabilities` are ignored. A `required` entry needs evidence,
never auto-enrolled from what a wrapper currently reports: a passing CI lane, or, only for a measured
capability no lane here could observe, a code reading, in which case CI is what proves it.
When an SDK gains support for an excepted capability, move it from `unsupported` to `required`.

`measuredCapabilities` are not read from the wrapper: the orchestrator measures them (here, the Accept-Encoding the SDK sends to the context server) and checks the result against this policy exactly like an advertised capability, so a reviewed exception that starts measuring true fails the run until it is moved to `required`.

capabilities.switchback: R33 cluster-defined switchback serving (ordered switchbackClusters, switchbackClusterValues) through a context, plus POST /switchback/assign and /switchback/permutation, advertised from a behavioral self-test
capabilities.diagnostics: POST /diagnostic hashUnit, computed by the SDK's own hashing
capabilities.diagnosticsUtf8: POST /diagnostic utf8Bytes, computed by the SDK's own UTF-8 encoder
capabilities.publishFail: POST /context/{id}/publishFail arms a one-shot publisher failure
capabilities.variableKeysMap: POST /context/{id}/variableKeysMap returns every experiment per variable key
capabilities.globalCustomFieldKeys: POST /context/{id}/globalCustomFieldKeys returns the union of custom field keys
capabilities.readyError: POST /context/{id}/readyError reports the error of a failed context
capabilities.holdouts: two-arm holdout resolution, advertised from a behavioral self-test
capabilities.holdout_arms: three-arm holdout resolution, advertised from a behavioral self-test
capabilities.assignmentRules: custom assignment rules: an experiment's assignmentRules string is evaluated and a matching rule wins with a ruleOverride:true exposure (advertised from a behavioral self-test)
capabilities.semverOperators: semver_eq/gt/gte/lt/lte operators in audience filters, compared numerically and locale-independently (advertised from a behavioral self-test)
capabilities.numericUnitIds: a numeric unit uid keeps its numeric JSON type end to end: getUnit/getUnits return the number the unit was set with (12345), not a stringified copy ("12345")
capabilities.publishThrowsOnFailure: a direct publish() call whose collector/transport fails surfaces the failure to the caller by throwing; the pending events are preserved and an error event is logged
capabilities.trackRejectsNonObjectProperties: track() rejects non-object goal properties (e.g. a list of pairs or an empty list) by throwing "Goal '<name>' properties must be of type object.", matching the JS reference
capabilities.refreshNoOpOnFailedContext: refresh() on a context whose initial load failed is a no-op: it does not fetch, emits no refresh or error event, the context stays failed, and data offered for the refresh is not applied (matching the JS reference)
capabilities.clientNoEnvironment: the wrapper can build a context whose client reports no environment (the optional client field on POST /context with environment omitted), so the SDK leaves environment out of the audience/rule evaluation map (the 2026-11 system-attributes 'no environment configured' case, scenario 253). SDKs whose public client API mandates a non-empty environment cannot express this black-box; their own unit tests cover it, so they list a reviewed exception
capabilities.xAgentHeader: the SDK's own requests carry X-Agent: absmartly-<lang>-sdk/<version> (the feature-parity round); the wrapper records the requests its mock collector serves (GET /context_payload/{id}/requests) and, with publishToEndpoint on POST /context, publishes through the SDK's own publisher to PUT {endpoint}/context
capabilities.clientRejectsBlankApplication: the SDK's client rejects an explicitly blank application at construction, and the wrapper forwards client.application unchanged on POST /context, so a blank name returns the SDK's own validation error as a 400 instead of being repaired into the wrapper's default (WRAPPER_API_SPEC.md, POST /context client)
capabilities.clientAcceptsBlankApplication: the SDK's client accepts an explicitly blank application and leaves application out of the audience/rule evaluation map; the wrapper forwards client.application unchanged on POST /context rather than repairing it into its default (WRAPPER_API_SPEC.md, POST /context client)
capabilities.throwsOnMisuse: misuse surfaces to the caller as an error, as in the JS reference: setUnit with a blank or already-set uid, a mutation (track/attribute/setUnit/treatment) after finalize, and a read before the context is ready throw (or return the SDK's idiomatic error) instead of only logging it; the wrapper maps that error to a 400 carrying the SDK's own message
capabilities.singleFinalizeEvent: sealing the context (finalize) logs exactly one lifecycle event, `finalize`, as in the JS reference; the wrapper returns every event the SDK logs, unrenamed and not de-duplicated
capabilities.semverNumericOperands: a numeric semver_* operand is converted to a string like the JS reference (toFixed(15), trailing zeros trimmed), so 1e-7 compares as 0.0000001 (scenario 332)
capabilities.contextFetchCompression: the SDK's own GET {endpoint}/context advertises gzip (Accept-Encoding) on create and refresh and decodes the gzip body; measured by the orchestrator on the context server, never self-reported
capabilities.contextFetchBrotli: the SDK's own GET {endpoint}/context advertises br (Accept-Encoding) on create and refresh and decodes the br body the context server then serves (a payload allowing br > gzip > identity), including the refreshed data; measured by the orchestrator on the context server, never self-reported
